newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury softens market leadership pursuit.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury softens market leadership pursuit.

text.p: British supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc indicated on Wednesday it would not pursue arch-rival and biggest seller Tesco at all costs as chief executive Dino Adriano said market share leadership was not the sole aim.
"I am not setting market share leadership as a goal (on its own)...I will not go blindly to market share at any price," he told journalists at a news conference.

Earlier, Sainsbury, which was knocked off the top slot over a year ago by Tesco, said annual profits slid 15 percent to 651 million stg and paid out a dividend of 12.3 pence, up from 12.1 pence, per share.

The company said supermarket sales from existing stores were up 4.2 percent in the early weeks of the current year compared with an increase of four percent in the 16 weeks to January 11, although sales in the key Christmas period were up 4.4 percent.
"I consider that rebuilding our superiority in quality and choice is the key to maintaining our sales and market share momentum," Adriano said.
He said Sainsbury's market share was 12.6 percent last year, up from 12.5 percent, compared with Tesco's 15 percent, up from 13.9 percent previously.
Adriano said the group aimed to make itself "the best food outlet in this country," differentiating from its competitors on range of goods on offer and service.
Sainsbury said that the costs of service improvements and its Reward loyalty card, which now accounts for 80 percent of sales, were 0.75 percent of sales on an ongoing basis.
Adriano added that gross margins were currently stable and there was "no indication that this is likely to change in the near future."
